faces.f: After millennia asleep, the Eldrazi had forgotten about Zendikar's fiery temper and dislike of strangers.

"Well, how could I know they'd explode?"
—Gregel, township militia
"The enemy is getting too close! Quick! Inflate the toad!"
"The best way over the mountain is through."
Only the Cabal could make a fight to the death more deadly.
He wants to watch Ravnica burn, one soul at a time.

"If you live on a giant's back, there's only one individual you'll ever need to fear."
—Gaddock Teeg
A cyclops has two moods: angry and asleep.
It traps an explosion within its stony skin.

"You have to appreciate the genius of it. Why bother building defenses when you can just fill the pass with angry ogres?"
—Javad Nasrin, Ondu relic hunter
The Keldons used the toxic vents in the cracked earth to bolster their home's defenses.

"Unwelcome thoughts crowd my mind. Are they my own madness, or the whispers of another?"
—Sarkhan Vol

"Do you hear that, Sarkhan? The glory of the horde! I made a legend from what you abandoned."
—Zurgo, khan of the Mardu
Kolaghan archers are trained in Dakla, the way of the bow. They utilize their dragonlord's lightning to strike their target, no matter how small, how fast, or how far away.

"Monsters dwell in every heart. We only think civilization tames them."
―Euphemia, Nexus watcher

"The gods used their feathers to paint all the colors of the world."
—Yare-Tiva, warden of Gramur Forest
Magistrate Ludy agreed to designate land for the brushstriders only after several broken windows and dozens of missing blini-cakes.
The first vine shows the others where to grow.
Fangren spur may sound louder, but Viridian resurgents claim that the horn of the vorrac creates a truer, more inspiring note.
Torching Krosa would be pointless. It grows faster than it burns.

"Are the gods angry at our discontent with what they give us, or jealous that we made a thing they cannot?"
—Kleon the Iron-Booted
Its blood is life. Its body is growth.
The baloth's instincts boiled, its muscles pulled taut, and its razor-spines bristled, as it turned to face—a runt meepling.

"Which is more filled with poison: the flower of the moonglove or the minds of elves?"
—Vessifrus, flamekin demagogue
Victory favors neither the righteous nor the wicked. It favors the prepared.
Urak froze when he heard it. That was his first mistake. He turned and cast a dramatic ward spell. That was his last.
It's not the two heads you should fear. It's the four fangs.
It is an expert at culling individuals who stray too far from the herd.
Nature doesn't walk.
The elf's blade carved deep into the Eldrazi drone's fleshy lattices. Without a sound, the drone lost equilibrium and tumbled from the sky.

"You don't find many old werewolf hunters."
—Paulin, trapper of Somberwald
Hunger makes a leucrocota dangerous. A full belly makes it angry and dangerous.

"The hermit dies. The outcast dies. The lone wolf dies. Only those who stick together survive this world."
—Uros, Pendelhaven elder
"None can own the land's bounty. The gods made this world for all to share its riches. And I'm not just saying that because you caught me stealing your fruit."
"Fair fight? How could it be a fair fight? We're Akroans. They're not."
A lawmage's runic script is an act of governance given form: legislation written directly onto the air itself.
Not the foulest or bloodiest act at Rix Maadi by a stretch.
Snaking remnants of nature directed by a body of thought and progress, the oracles embody all that is Simic.
Swarms thrive in its nest, feeding on leathery bits of discarded wing.

"We are the heart of the wild, the fire in its eyes, and the howl in its throat. Come, join the battle to which you were born."
—Kroshkar, Gruul shaman
To protect the alliance between Kjeldor and Yavimaya, they trained in the ways of both.
"The direst venom becomes a panacea under Pharika's guidance. I bring it to the worthy, clinging at the edge of the abyss."

The Champion stood alone between the horde of the Returned and the shrine to Karametra, cutting down scores among hundreds. She would have been overcome if not for the aid of the temple guardians whom Karametra awakened.
—*The Theriad*
The hedrons awoke along with the Eldrazi, forming superstructures that radiated overwhelming magic.

"Use everything. Iron, rust, scrap . . . even the ground must join our cause."
—Ezuri, renegade leader

"Rath grows, and I am nourished."
—Volrath
Kitesailing is a way of life—and without practice, the end of it.
Purphoros once loved Nylea, the god of the hunt. His passion inspired his most astounding works of art.
She is the apex of the artificer's craft, the spirit of the divine called out of base metal.

"If that brain can't figure out the secret of the serum, then add more brains."
—Rhmir, Hand of the Augur
Scholars had puzzled for centuries over the ruins at Tal Terig. Its secrets had always lived within one rune-carved head.
The last reliable landmark in Tazeem just walked away.
Without the interfering hands of civilization, nature will always shape itself to its own needs.

"It was a strange morning. When we awoke, we found our trees transformed. We didn't know whether to water them or polish them."
—Pulan, Bant orchardist
Rumors quickly spread among thieves about a labyrinth without walls and a prize beyond all measures of worth.
Untold riches await those who forsake the bustling world to search the secret, silent places.
"The beneficent council deems you worthy of favor. They hope this doesn't provoke envy from your peers."
"In the market for an alternative, friend?"

"Unusual. Security also worth stealing."
—Dack Fayden
On Fiora, no matter is settled until King Brago offers an opinion.
When its power is threatened, the council speaks with a unified voice.
"We remember. We rise."
"The Black Rose doesn't tolerate weeds."
"Secrets, like coins, are easy to steal."
"Your defiance is noted."
When every right is voted away, only rage remains.
"Their guards are soft, ready to welcome a sharp dagger."

"Everything comes with a price. Especially revolution."
—Grenzo, dungeon warden

"And Muzzio says my arguments have no teeth."
—Selvala, ranger of the Lowlands
Selvala's arrival never goes unnoticed.
"My rule persists beyond death itself."

"All who set foot in Paliano are pawns in someone's play for power."
—Marchesa, the Black Rose
If you want to wreak havoc above, sometimes it's best to look below.
Those who can't conspire, create.
"Watch your head . . . and your back."
"The Lowlands refuse to suffer at the whims of the High City."
Why wait for answers?
Paliano's creations provide ample opportunities to plot the downfall of a neighbor.
Each volume contains wonders.
Spy for today. Plan for tomorrow.
"Ajani goes where he is needed most and in his name we keep his lands safe."
The Orzhov started using hawks as messengers in order to bypass the many toll roads and bridges that dot Ravnica. Soon the service became one of their most profitable businesses.
He vowed he would never rest until he reached his destination. He doesn't know how right he was.
In life, they were a motley crew: farmers, lords, cutpurses, priests. In death, they are united in singular, benevolent purpose.
Sacred rites repurposed to fight an ancient threat.
"My faith is stronger than fang, claw, or mindless hunger."

"May starving fleas birth a thousand generations on your stubborn hide, cow!"
—Bruse Tarl, Goma Fada nomad
"Any hotheaded cub can raise a sword in anger."
"You have not died until I consent."

"End this. What I seek is far greater."
—Elesh Norn, Grand Cenobite

"Be careful in your hunt. The clever little creature can steal your wards and lead you right into the werewolf's den."
—Britta, midwife of Gatstaf
"Their spirits walk the winds and fill my soul."

"Just a moment of perfect grace and sanctity is enough."
—Kal Lior, leonin elder
The smallest seed of regret can bloom into redemption.
After Gideon cleansed the Ninth District, none of the ganglords challenged the Boros.
"As my father taught, 'Training will raise your shield to the blow, but courage fills the gaps the shield leaves open.'"

"I prefer loyalty to be a matter of respect, not of magic. But one does what one must."
—Kaalia of the Vast
Its pulsating cry shatters bonds of iron, granite, and servitude.

"The wind smells of misfortune. Check your knots."
—Anitan, Ondu cleric

"Wind is forceful, yet ephemeral. It can knock a dragon out of the sky, yet pass through the smallest crack unhindered."
—Jestus Dreya, *Of Elements and Eternity*
The mizzium-sphere array drove her mind deep into the thought field, where only the rarest motes of genius may be plucked.
The ideas came flooding in so fast that they couldn't all be contained.
"Four parts molten bronze, yes . . . one part frozen mercury, yes, yes . . . but then what?"

"Creation is a paradox. It hatches from its opposite."
—Olka, Mistmeadow witch
"Try to pretend like you understand what's important."
Long thought to be extinct, flocks of gryffs reappeared with Avacyn's return.
"It's simple, really. If they can't find us, they can't kill us."
The bolt struck with a flash, and there was a terrible sound, as of glass shattering, but the creature was unharmed.
The scrollkeepers never stepped an inch away from the doors of the Great Library, not even when the ogres and their oni masters swept through Minamo.
The Neurok buried entangling cables just under the Quicksilver Sea. One seastrider harvest can provide an army's worth of armor and shields.
"Any good prospector must sift the gold from the sand."
The Simic created the cells to preserve their experiments. The Azorius put the cells to use on the guilty.

"Superior force meets woefully inadequate object. What paradox were you expecting?"
—Azguri, archmage of Evos Isle

"Let their mindless armies come and face the might of genius."
—Varil, Neurok partisan
"Take my hand and dance to the music of the winds."

"Don't worry, your death will be as informative as possible."
—Gorghul, augur of skulls

"This is how wars are won—not with armies of soldiers but with a single knife blade, artfully placed."
—Yurin, royal assassin
Urza thought it a crusade. Xantcha knew it was a robbery.
Not once in the history of Grixis has anyone died of old age.

"The finest minions know what I need without me ever saying a thing."
—Liliana Vess
"Behold! The image of the enemy and all that she has. Trust your envy, and take it."

"Let go your grudges, or risk wandering the bogs forever in a murderous rage."
—Hildin, priest of Avacyn

"Look at her, once filled with innocence. Death has a way of wringing away such . . . deficiencies."
—Savra
"The end is justified in being mean. Or something like that."
His family was a small price to pay for the dark gifts that called to him.
Take away a few things, and a rebellion may ensue. Take away everything, and the oppression will be accepted as fate.
In Urborg, the instigators of each new rebellion are soaked in the blood of the last.
As Phage drank their energy, a vague memory of Jeska stirred. Then she lost herself again in the joy of her victims' suffering.
Linger on death's door and risk being invited in.
Kidnappers caught in Havengul are given two choices: languish in prison or become rat catchers. The smart ones go to prison.
Agreements with demons seldom end at the grave.
When the blood hunt lost its thrill, she looked for less tangible means of domination.

"Die. But die knowing that your pathetic life will yield a great bounty for me."
—Zul Ashur, lich lord
Hers is an ancient form of necromancy, steeped in shamanic trance and ritual that few skaberen or ghoulcallers comprehend.

"Removing the encumbrance of useless brain tissue grants several advantages: a slight increase in mobility, a response of revulsion and horror from the enemy, and, in the case of large specimens, room for passengers."
—Zul Ashur, lich lord
Fervid shamans willingly submit to shockers in hopes of glimpsing the fortunes of the future.
"Now everyone knows what you are."

"The smell of roasted flesh hung over the valley for hours."
—Onean sergeant
A flame-kin is always formidable, but feeding its fire with a sorcerous gift grants it the power to devastate armies.

"Remember the fable of the elf who came upon a cave of gold. In trying to free the largest piece, she was crushed by its weight."
—Karn
Hidetsugu held over a dozen oni in blood oath. At his touch, rocks scorched. At his word, cities burned.
Their language may be a cacophonous agglomeration of chittering snorts and mad barking, but the message they send is all too clear.
Don't let its appearance frighten you. Let its claws and teeth do that.
The Quicksilver Sea hissed and bubbled at the indignity. The Vulshok shaman just smiled.

"Crispy! Scarback! Load another volcano-ball."
—Stumphobbler Thuj, orcish captain
The ingenuity of goblins, the depravity of demons, and the smarts of sheep.
The cinders believe their flame was stolen by one they call the Extinguisher. All who now wield fire draw their desperate wrath.
Devils redecorate every room with fire.
Keldon warriors don't need signals to tell them when to attack. They need signals to tell them when to stop.

"Zendikar fortifies itself against the Great Threat, making sentries of sky, sea, and stone."
—*The War Diaries*

"How can we outrun the sky?"
—Hadran, sunseeder of Naya

"Our pyromancer's flames may not have killed them, but they bought us the time we needed."
—*The War Diaries*

"Is it wrong to go straight for what you want? Sneaking is for cats and goblins."
—Tahngarth of the *Weatherlight*
Fangren spur may sound louder, but Viridian resurgents claim that the horn of the vorrac creates a truer, more inspiring note.
A single seed unleashes a flurry of growth.
Nature's strength outlives the strong.

"Only when we journey into the unknown can we find the impossible."
—Cyrul the Wanderer

"Werewolves are an unholy mix of a predator's instinct and a human's hatred."
—Alena, trapper of Kessig

"We should learn from the hydra. It never plays favorites; it devours everyone equally."
—Thrass, elder druid

"The timeless, tireless jaws of nature shall one day devour us all."
—Sildark, artificer of Omu
It eats what it wants to eat—which is anything that moves.

"Let nothing own the skies but the wind."
—Dejara, Giltwood druid

"Never start a fight you can't finish."
—Padril, council guardian
There are many ruins, but there used to be many more.
"If they board us we're finished," warned Orim. Crovax nodded. "And if they don't . . . what then?"
Slain warriors were buried with a tree sapling, so they would become a part of the forest after death.
The wurms become so big, a single scale can be used as a roof for a human dwelling.

"They don't move much, but then again, if you get caught in its web, it has all the time in the world to get to you."
—Saidah, Joraga hunter
In the treetops, unseen by many, lurks chittering, skittering death.
Some nature mages unknowingly took advantage of the temporal energies still swirling on Dominaria. What they mistook for healing magic was in fact the manipulation of time.
"Why listen to the mumblings of wizards when the lash speaks true?"
Anarchy comes in many forms: social, individual, Gruul . . .
"Fear not. Your life will not go unlived."
"I am not at liberty to reveal my sources, but I can assure you, the price on your head is high."
Yavimaya lights the quickest path to battle.
The land drank power from the Mirari as though it had thirsted forever.
Many who cross Sorin's path come down with a sudden and fatal case of being-in-the-way-of-a-millennia-old-vampire.
"Yawgmoth," Freyalise whispered as she set the bomb, "now you will pay for your treachery."

"Like a strain of music: easy to remember but impossible to catch."
—Mirri of the *Weatherlight*
"Heat of battle" is usually a metaphor.

"It is not that you will go mad. It is that you will beg for madness."
—Volrath

"The Vanished must have sent it from beyond to aid us in this struggle."
—Kessla, Sylvok shaman
Lanterns carved from the mystic stones of the Reito Mines were said to light the way of lost souls.
Scholars had puzzled for centuries over the ruins at Tal Terig. Its secrets had always lived within one rune-carved head.
Scholars say that arbiters exist on every world, created by an unknown hand to enforce justice.
The first searchlights were given as gifts, symbols of cooperation, to the emissaries present at the signing of the Guildpact.
The model incorporated the fifth sun effortlessly, as if it had always known.
The best defense is a good offense.
Not all deaths are etched with mythic meaning and iconic glory.
Does it reflect the future that once was or the past that can never be?
They are cautious with their body language and facial expressions. Any stray movement could betray the positions of the troops they protect and cost many lives.
As his new wings lifted him high above Bant, Taric felt his earthly aspirations transform into heavenly resolve.
When the meek charge into battle, courage becomes infectious.

"The bird wore the form of a man, bereft of filigree. Why do the Texts not speak of it?"
—Belator of Esper

"This new chaos confounds us. We must fling it into our winds, our storms. These we can control."
—Bezzit Plar, Esper stormcaller
Mages of Esper measure their wealth and status by the number of servants in their retinues.
It shines in the darkness of its master's ambitions.
Without a connection of mind and body, magic is just an idea stuck in the head, a word on the tip of a tongue.
A paragon of honor, Galo Aher fell to a blast of fire. The Order of the White Orchid was so saddened that they forged a new sigil in his likeness.
Their war forgotten, the nations of Bant stood united in the face of a common threat.
"If I had many lives, I would give them all for Bant."
"We must hunt and kill the dragon before it can return to raze our ancient city."
"Let my lance sing with the voices of angels and the heathen cower before my shield, for I will teach this land the meaning of honor."
The weight of her conviction balances on the harmony of her soul.

"Whether or not you will bow to me is not open to debate. The question is, will I ever let you rise?"
—Fridius, telemin master
When Asha left Bant, she ensured that the world would have protection and order in her absence.
As the outsiders invaded Bant, soldiers who once saw sigils as the highest marks of glory began to see the scars of battle as tokens of equal worth.
The lives of elves are long, but their memories are longer. Even after death, they do not desert their homes.
Priests of Bant protect their temples with traps more elaborate than any mosaic floor.
Togk Manytooth struggled helplessly as the kathari circled above him. For a warrior, immobilization is a fate worse than death.

"The stone is more potent than ever. The flesh that creeps into our land will become even more slovenly and weak."
—Niclavs, archmage of Esper
The more metal it digests, the more its jelly will fetch on the alchemists' market.
Esper mages devised their weapons to be so devastating that war seemed unnecessary.
The battle was won in the commander's head before the first weapon was drawn.
"It's simple, really. If they can't find us, they can't kill us."

"Into its maw went the seventh sea, never to be seen again while the world remains."
—Esper fable
"Wasted potential surrounds us. Lend me that bauble, and let me see what it can be made to be."
After finding no sustenance on the edges of Grixis, it turned to the skies of Bant.

"The road to truth has many branches, and so must the cane with which I walk it."
—Voln the Elder

"With no flesh, there is no pain, no hesitation, no emotion of any kind. He is crafted perfection."
—Tezzeret

"Send it back to its own strange world so we can avoid another inglorious combat with these wicked beings."
—Captain Valek of Jhess
"This air feels so heavy and thick. There are no winds to speak of. I fear the knowledge that comes from a place like this."
Every horizon hides a new possibility.
The bones of Jund's dead resurfaced in Naya, poisoning the jungle and killing the sunseeders' crops.
The barbarians of Jund believe the bottomless tar pits extend forever into other, darker worlds.
Dreadwings spring from lofty perches to surprise kathari in midflight. They smother their prey and then consume it as they glide gently toward the ground.
Necromancers who discovered the new sources of mana were quick to dream up new nightmares with them.
Not once in the history of Grixis has anyone died of old age.
When the smell of passing thoughts piques its hunger, its maw becomes primed with acid and a taste for brains.
Born of volcanic forces, it thrives on the absolute panic it inspires.
Esper artificers never imagined that one day their scraps would be pressed against their soft and fragile throats.
One goes to Tidehollow either to forget or to be forgotten. Either way, the scullers will oblige.
The problem with a liquid that can dissolve anything is finding something to carry it in.
As Grixis collided with the rest of Alara, the worlds began to hear the hateful whispers of the forgotten dead.

"The meek inherit nothing."
—Sedris, the Traitor King
The demon's yoke is part leash, part noose.
For Sarkhan Vol, the dragon is the purest expression of life's savage splendor.
A drop of blood spilled from the first dragon.
On Jund, the deep canyons were the best places to hide. When the goblins wandered into Naya, they found that was not so true.
When you've got the temperament of a dragon, every argument is one you'll win.
The farther he roamed from Jund and its dragons, the more he felt their essence in himself.
Jund feasts on the unprepared.
Finding themselves in a new and unexplored world, they immediately set it on fire.
"Bant is a world imprisoned by polished stone and tyrannical rule. It yearns to strike back against those who restrain it."

"A surly beast, the kranioceros will raise its defenses at the smallest threat. Stay out of sight and downwind, or you'll disrupt its natural migrations."
—Ebrel, godtoucher mentor
The spikes of sangrite made the goblin stronger, but they didn't make him any smarter.
The metal filigree in his body glowed red-hot, and his flesh soon followed.
You'd better know how to pray for rain.

"The finest pawns are those with pawns of their own."
—Nicol Bolas
There are no "weak" creatures on Jund. Even the smallest can strike a deadly blow.
"I'll fight two at once, and then lick their guts from my blades."

"How can we outrun the sky?"
—Hadran, sunseeder of Naya
Tired of waiting for a dragon to eat them, some hardy goblins struck out to become meals for the unknown.
When its smoky plumes light Naya's sky, every creature from the smallest pip fawn to the largest rannet heeds the warning.
It's revered for its power, celebrated for its grace, and feared for the avalanches triggered by its thunderous feet.
"The sun shines bright upon the strong."

"Each night, the sun unravels and blows away. Each day, the spiders set a new one in the sky."
—Sunseeder myth
The sphinx tyrannized Bant until a rhox mage tested the hardiness of her shiny parts.
On Jund, everything eventually ends up in something else's stomach.
When outsiders interrupted the matca championship, things got ugly.
The combined strength of all five planes spawned creations none had seen before.

"Blades dull and armor dents. Marisi taught us that instinct is the only thing a true warrior needs."
—Ajani
She protects the sacred groves from blight, drought, and the Unbeholden.

"Gods do not sleep soundly in the earth's embrace."
—Mayael the Anima
"Our arrows are aimed not at the sacred behemoths but at those who dare to dream of such a trophy."
To train her elves for war, Mayael would drop a sackful of acorns from the tree canopy. Each archer tried to split as many as possible before the acorns hit the forest floor below.
Alara is broken no more.
An avatar he sculpts of wisdom and strength.
Seeds from Jund don't drift gently on the wind. They get up and stampede.
Some who scouted new lands chose to stay.
Jund's thallids tried to disguise their deliciousness by covering themselves in spines harvested from the tukatongue tree.

"Leotau that were born wild make the best mounts. It's like riding a thunderstorm."
—Rafiq of the Many
Jund's dragons hoard only sangrite crystals. Its wurms aren't so picky.
The progeny of the Maelstrom shows no allegiance—and no mercy—to any of the five shards.
After years of world-bending machinations, Bolas's triumph is at hand.
Each of the twenty-three winds of Esper is named and chronicled, and every possible interaction with the flow of magic is exhaustively detailed.
Taste his power, hunger for his command.

"The smiths of this land must be mad to reach so far and so high for another creature to decorate."
—Cagen Vargan, Jhessian sea scout
Reuniting a world is not a gentle process.
As the shards merged into the Maelstrom, their mana energies fused into new monstrosities.
"To trespass so far from home is to ask for a lonesome grave."
Egbol stared in wonder at Naya's landscape. So much to eat. So much to steal.
"Everyone has a price."
A killing machine from birth.
"You have two choices: heed my advice now or need my healing later."

"Knowledge of Bant's landscape and ruins is a weapon that the invaders can't comprehend."
—Elspeth
The elves of Naya were the last to acknowledge the massive shift of mana in their world.
There is no world where angels fear to tread.
"These benighted worlds are thick with ignorance. I will educate them. They will listen, or they will die."
A demon cannot be trusted, and a dragon will not be ruled.
When the shards merged, Mayael found herself the general of Naya's mightiest army.
Survival in the wilds of Naya left Tiyan well equipped to win the civilized battles of Bant.
The Soul of the World has returned.
An enlightened soul caged in a body made for battle.

"There is only one way of life in Jund: feed on the weak until you are cut down by something stronger."
—Jorshu of Clan Nel Toth
They lament the doom that is coming to Bant without realizing the part their own leaders have played in it.
Underneath the cities of Esper are cycles of life unseen by those who feed them.

"They think they're winning. But they're just lining up to be dinner."
—Rakka Mar
Plowbeasts of Naya escaped their harnesses in droves, content to snack on the conveniently cultivated fields of Eos and Valeron.
After years of honing her philosophy in debate with stubborn rhoxes, Niella was ready to convert any heathen.
With their life energy suppressed under their etherium enhancements, thieves from Esper found it surprisingly easy to explore the ruins of Grixis.
The Seekers of Carmot searched across the unknown lands for the mystical red stone that could reforge Esper in ethereal perfection.
The ripe smell of life drifted into Grixis. The dead caught the scent and with reckless hunger followed it back into Jund.
The mysterious purpose of two of the rings had eluded Esper mages—until now.
In a world where death is always violent, cruel weapons are as common as rocks.
Those who drink from Malfegor's cup are tainted with hunger and stained with lies.
Once broken, who knows what worlds might grow from its shards?
Those who dismiss the cylix as an ordinary wooden bowl are blind to the true measure of its worth.
As the shards merged, relics once thought mundane regained forgotten powers.
Built in honor of Alara's creatures, the ziggurat vanished long ago. When Progenitus awakened, the temple emerged again.

"It was a strange morning. When we awoke, we found our trees transformed. We didn't know whether to water them or polish them."
—Pulan, Bant orchardist
When the aven scouts located the tower in Esper, the Knights of the Reliquary set off on a righteous crusade to recover their lost treasures.
The goblins went to sleep in Jund and awoke in Grixis. They'd never seen a zombie before. They would never see one again.
Drink deep, and know the path to the heart of the wilds.
"Time is fluid as a dance, and truth as fleeting."
Destiny exalts a chosen few, but even heroes break.
"I don't know where my destiny lies, but I know it isn't here."

"Every choice alters the path of fate."
—Sarkhan Vol

"The bane of countless shattered weapons, each a failure to slay her."
—Daghatar the Adamant
The mere approach of an Abzan war beast is enough to send enemies fleeing in panic.
That which endures, survives.
She doesn't escort the dead to the afterlife, but instead raises them to fight and die again.

"More than snow falls from the Boreal skies."
—Arkin Egilsson, skycaptain

"With his dream of unification fulfilled, Darien became the last king of Kjeldor. Those who followed were known as the kings of New Argive."
—*Kjeldor: Ice Civilization*
The Knights of Stromgald struck Darien's Roost from two sides. They would have caught Kjeldor in a pincer attack were it not for Darien's tacticians.
The gargoyles were taken from the walls of flooded Kjeldoran cities and brought upland to guard the outposts of New Argive.
"I listen to people. He sniffs the wind. And we both sense something big coming. Something very big."
King Darien's breath crystallized and fell to the frozen battlefield, but its command carried true to all soldiers of New Argive.

"The White Shield is not the burnished metal you lash to your forearm but the conviction that burns in your chest."
—Lucilde Fiksdotter, leader of the Order of the White Shield
"Only in our vulnerability is there true power, and that power is life itself."
The aberrant magic of the Rimewind drew the unicorns back from the northern wastes to do battle once again.

"The scouts claim the cold has malice, and a mind. I begin to believe them. Impassable drifts seem to appear before us at every turn."
—Aevar Borg, northern guide, journal entry

The unfortunates so transformed hungered not for flesh, but for warmth.

"Tresserhorn is ours now. Dredge the lake and bring me all the bones you find. We'll build you a new army, the likes of which Terisiare has never seen."

"Let your heartbeat be the thunder in the valley. Let your swords be the lightning on the peaks."
—Lothar Lovisason, Balduvian chieftain
"To a trained mind, the cold is but a momentary distraction."

"They're not easily trained. Fortunately, they already know how to kill."
—Lovisa Coldeyes, Balduvian chieftain

"Weep not for me. I will rise with the spring's new growth."

—*The Dynasty of Winter Kings*

"Our noble land, enslaved by Rime,

"Our land oppressed by silent Cold,
